sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the superiority of the fifteenth of Av over other fifteenths of the month is because its ascent follows the great descent of Tisha B'Av, and this descent into physicality enables the greatest ascent, even surpassing Yom Kippur.

translations.translation: And the point of explanation regarding the superiority of the fifteenth of Av,
even though on every fifteenth of the month there is a fullness of the moon,
is explained in the discourses,
that this is because the ascent of the fifteenth of Av comes after the descent of Tisha B'Av.
And the concept is,
behold, it is stated in the Yalkut,
"A lion arose in the constellation of the lion and destroyed Ariel... on condition that a lion would come"
[this is the Holy One, blessed be He, of Whom it is written,
"A lion has roared, who will not fear"],
"in the constellation of the lion"
["and I will turn their mourning into joy"],
"and he will build Ariel, etc."
And this means,
that the exile and destruction that was in the constellation of the lion
(in the fifth month)
was solely in order
(on condition)
that a lion would come, etc., and build Ariel,
the third Holy Temple,
which is more elevated than the First and Second Temples.
For the superiority of the third Holy Temple
(which is more elevated than the First Temple and than the Second Temple)
comes specifically through the precedence of exile, etc.
And this is
the superiority of the fifteenth of Av over the fifteenth of every month,
even over the fifteenth of Nissan
(Pesach)
and the fifteenth of Tishrei
(Sukkot),
because since the ascent of the fifteenth of Av comes after the great descent of Tisha B'Av
("a lion arose, etc., and destroyed Ariel"),
therefore it is a most exceedingly great ascent.
And as is known,
the general principle regarding ascents and descents,
that according to the measure of the descent, so is the ascent.
And even though the ascent of the fifteenth of Nissan
(Pesach)
also came after the descent of the Egyptian exile,
nevertheless, at that time Israel were in a state and condition of tzaddikim.
And also the ascent of the fifteenth of Tishrei
(Sukkot),
even though it comes in the aftermath of the repentance of Yom Kippur,
nevertheless,
since the entirety of the service of Torah and mitzvos is a spiritual service
[for even though the mitzvos are clothed in physical things,
tzitzis in physical wool and tefillin in physical parchment,
nevertheless, the essence of the mitzvos is to bring spirituality into physicality],
behold, the descent caused by sins and transgressions
(the opposite of the essence of the mitzvos)
is in relation to physicality as it pertains to spirituality,
and consequently, this is not yet the ultimate descent,
and therefore also the ascent of Sukkot through repentance is not the ultimate ascent.
However, the descent of Tisha B'Av,
when "He poured out His wrath on the wood and on the stones"
(physical wood and stones),
meaning that the descent
(from the side of sins)
affected the physicality of the world, which has no lower level beneath it,
behold, since the descent of Tisha B'Av is a descent beneath which there is none,
therefore also the ascent of the fifteenth of Av that follows this descent is a most exceedingly great ascent,
according to the measure of the intensity of the descent.
And this is the concept of "double consolation,"
"I, I am He Who comforts you,"
a double "Anochi."
Based on this, it is understood that the festival of the fifteenth of Av is more elevated even than the festival of Yom Kippur.
And this is what they said, "There were no greater festivals for Israel than the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur,"
that it places the fifteenth of Av before Yom Kippur,
even though the concept of the fifteenth of Av
(according to all the reasons in the Gemara)
was innovated many years after Yom Kippur,
and also in the times of the year
(in every year)
Yom Kippur
(which is in the month of Tishrei)
precedes the fifteenth of Av,
because the festival of the fifteenth of Av is more elevated
(preceding in level)
than the festival of Yom Kippur.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the superiority of the fifteenth of Av over other festivals stems from the fact that its fullness of the moon comes from the service of Israel that is above the Torah, unlike the fullness of the moon on Pesach and Sukkot which comes from service within the Torah's measure.

translations.translation: But still, it needs to be understood,
behold, "And you shall rejoice in your festival" is a positive commandment from the Torah,
unlike the festival
(and the joy)
of the fifteenth of Av.
And also the festival of Yom Kippur is not from the Torah
[for there is no obligation to rejoice on Yom Kippur,
and on the contrary,
the commandment of Yom Kippur is "and you shall afflict your souls."
And only because it is a day of forgiveness and atonement,
behold, incidentally, the matter of joy is derived from this],
and if so, how is it possible that the festival
(and the joy)
of the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur could be greater than the festivals that are a commandment from the Torah to rejoice in them.
But the concept is,
that in the elevation of "the moon stands in its fullness," there are two aspects in general.
The aspect of "the moon stands in its fullness" as it is from the side of the order and law of the Torah
[and from this is derived the order of the changes of the moon according to nature],
and the aspect of "the moon stands in its fullness" as it is from the side of the service of man,
as it is above how it is according to the law of the Torah.
For Israel are above the Torah,
therefore Israel are called "groom" and the Torah is called "bride,"
because Israel are the bestowers upon the Torah.
For this is the concept of "Bless the Torah first,"
that Israel bless and draw down into the Torah from the aspect of the Giver of the Torah,
and in the manner of Dovid, who would connect the Torah with the Holy One, blessed be He.
And this is the superiority of the fifteenth of Av over the fifteenth of Nissan and the fifteenth of Tishrei,
for the fullness of the moon on the fifteenth of Nissan and the fifteenth of Tishrei is the concept of "the moon stands in its fullness" from the side of the order of the Torah,
meaning from the side of the service of man as it is in measure according to the Torah.
For even though through this service an elevation is made in the world,
nevertheless, the elevation is in measure and limitation.
However, the fullness of the moon on the fifteenth of Av is the concept of "the moon stands in its fullness" as it is from the side of the service of the souls of Israel that is above the Torah,
the service of "with all your might."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the three levels of the world—the world as it is, the addition through service within Torah measure, and the innovation through service above measure—using the verse "the advantage of the land is in everything; a king is served by the field."

translations.translation: And in order to explain these three matters
[the world as it is in itself,
"the world was created in its fullness."
What is added to the world through the service of man as it is from the side of the measure of the Torah.
And the innovation that is made through the service of "with all your might" that is above measure
(even from the measure of the Torah)],
the discourses bring
the explanation of the verse,
"And the advantage of the land is in everything; a king is served by the field,"
that there are three aspects in this.
The aspect of "land" as it is in itself,
the "advantage" of the land through the aspect of "everything,"
and the aspect of "a king is served by the field" which is more elevated than the "advantage of the land."
For behold, "the advantage of the land" is the aspect of "field"
(as it is in itself)
[for "field" is included in "land," except that because it is of the choicest part of the land,
that which is fit for sowing and growth,
therefore it is the "advantage of the land"],
however, that which "a king is served by the field"
(the elevation made in the field through service)
is above the "advantage of the land."
And the concept is,
behold, "field" refers to the Garden of Eden,
for just as a field is of the choicest part of the land, that which is fit for sowing and growth
(as above),
so too the Garden of Eden is of the choicest part of the world, that which is fit for the revelation of light,
meaning for the aspect of light that is above the light that shines in the entirety of the world.
For the light that shines in the entirety of the world is from the aspect of the midos,
for this is that which the coming into being is from the aspect of the six days of construction or the seven days of construction.
And even though the world was created with ten utterances
(in the ten are also included the three mochin),
behold, this is the mochin as they are within the midos.
But the light that shines in the Garden of Eden is
(also)
from the aspect of the three highest Sefiros.
And for this reason there is yet another superiority in the Garden of Eden over the entirety of the world,
that the revelation in the world is in the aspect of knowledge of existence,
and in the Garden of Eden it is a revelation of the essence.
And this is that "the advantage of the land, etc." is the aspect of the Garden of Eden
(and as above, "the advantage of the land" is the aspect of "field"),
for the Garden of Eden is the aspect of the world as it is a complete structure in all ten Sefiros,
seven lower Sefiros and three highest Sefiros,
the aspect of "the world was created in its fullness."
And this is also what is written, "And the advantage of the land is in everything,"
that the advantage
(and the superiority)
of the Garden of Eden over the entirety of the world is through "everything,"
"everything" refers to the Sefirah of Yesod
which is called "everything" because of the fifty gates of Binah
("everything" in gematria is fifty)
that are drawn down into it,
and through this there is also drawn down into it from the aspect of Chochmah,
for Chochmah and Binah are the entirety of the mochin.
And the aforementioned superiority of the Garden of Eden, that it is the "advantage of the land"
[that the aspect of the three highest Sefiros shines in it,
and because of this there is also in it a revelation of the essence]
is the aspect of "field" in itself.
However, through service,
"a king is served by the field,"
an elevation is made that is above the aspect of the "advantage of the land."
And as it is stated in the Zohar,
"A king is served by the field" — who is the king? This is the Supreme King,
that this aspect is above the world
(even as it is in perfection,
the "advantage of the land").
For the entire matter of the coming into being of the world is only from the ten utterances, the beginning of which is Chochmah,
and the Supreme King is the aspect of Kesser, which is above the chain of descent.
